item.title: Hakata Gion Yamakasa Festival — Guide
item.description: The Hakata Gion Yamakasa is Fukuoka’s most famous and thrilling festival, a tradition over 700 years old held every July, centred on Kushida Shrine. Over two weeks, ornate decorative floats (kazariyama) are displayed around the city, but the real drama is the racing floats (kakiyama) — one-tonne portable shrines carried on the shoulders of teams of men in traditional loincloths. It climaxes before dawn on July 15 with the ‘Oiyama’, when the teams charge a roughly 5-kilometre course through the streets of Hakata at a flat sprint, water thrown over them by cheering crowds, racing against the clock in a spectacle of raw energy, sweat and community pride.
